heading: Unlearning can bring target accuracy near chance, preserve general ability, and resist simple attacks
definition: a method brings targeted-knowledge accuracy to near chance while keeping general ability, and simple attacks don't recover it.
summary: Independent groups reproduce near-chance accuracy on the knowledge targeted for removal, with general ability largely preserved. Resistance to simple attacks is contested when these include fine-tuning on a few examples or edits made with access to the model's internals.

suggested_status.by_scale:
Toy: R0 with mixed results, from one study (2609.27593; counts have no toy bucket). With a frozen encoder, excision is undone by a white-box scalar patch. With a trainable encoder, the bias patch gives zero readout.

<1B: C, thin (counts: versions.A.studies_by_size['<1B'] = 9; coverage_by_operation.attack.by_size['<1B'] = 1). UNDO (2506.06278) and GRAM (2607.08077) show suppression quickly reversed by forget-domain fine-tuning. 2610.09004 (verdict limits_scope): the BERT-Tiny scrub relearns more slowly than a never-adapted control (252 vs 75 updates), but an exact Q/K rescale cuts recovery to 25 steps.

1-10B (studies_by_size['1-10B'] = 212; attack.by_size['1-10B'] = 51):
- Near-chance forgetting with MMLU kept is R2. For plain RMU on Zephyr-7B, other groups re-evaluate the original's released cais/Zephyr_RMU checkpoint (2409.18025, 2608.22527: one checkpoint, not separate runs), and 2408.06223 re-implements RMU on Zephyr. On other families, the other-group evidence is Adaptive RMU at selected early layers only: Yi-6B l=7, Llama-3-8B l=5 and Mistral-7B l=5 (2408.06223). Other early layers fail or cost MMLU. RMU on Llama-3-8B-Instruct (2408.15221) and ELM (2410.02760) come from studies that share authors with the WMDP original, so they count as R1.
- 'Simple attacks don't recover it' is C if few-example fine-tuning or white-box edits count as simple. On the released Zephyr RMU checkpoint, 5 forget-set examples, 10 retain-set examples or direction ablation recover it (2409.18025). Other groups recover other near-chance checkpoints by tampering or benign fine-tuning (2502.05209, 2411.12103, lw:LLebzjrxuRzji6zhk). The original itself reports that forget-corpus fine-tuning recovers WMDP-Cyber on Mistral-7B RMU (figure-only). 4-bit quantization recovers MUSE checkpoints that sat at retrain level, not near chance, and 8-bit does not (2410.16454).
- Prompt-based attacks mostly fail on the released checkpoint in other groups' hands: DIA, Crescendo and few-shot QA (2608.22527), and simple jailbreaks (2409.18025). Enhanced GCG on that checkpoint gives conflicting results: 29.9→53.9 (2409.18025) against 0.3166→0.3637 (2608.22527). Rephrasing and translation recover only partly (2411.12103, limits_scope). RepNoise, RR and K-FADE resist input-space attacks (2502.05209). Human multi-turn red teaming recovers 51.2% of 43 questions on RMU Llama-3-8B-Instruct, but that study shares authors with the original (2408.15221; R1).

10-100B (studies_by_size['10-100B'] = 26; attack.by_size['10-100B'] = 4):
- Forgetting with ability kept is R2 from PINT on Llama-3-70B (2611.03955), a different method; the checks flag no author overlap for it. ELM on Qwen2.5-32B and Llama3-70B (2410.02760) is R1, because the study shares an author with the WMDP original. The original's own Mixtral-8x7B row stays 9 points above chance (2403.03218#r5, verdict fix).
- Robustness leans C but rests on few studies. INT4 recovers NPO on Qwen3-32B (2608.04519). A 250M-token instruction SFT with life-science subsets removed returns Gemma 4 26B-A4B GD WMDP-Bio 28.6→77.4, against 78.8 for original+SFT. RMU on the same model goes 29.2→60.8, and the Cyber rebounds are partial (2610.25791). GRIP-constrained RMU on Qwen3-30B-A3B resists expert forcing, while unconstrained RMU does not (2601.16905). No other group in these records repeats the original's own GCG test (Yi-34B RMU).

>100B: R0 for forgetting only, from one inference-time study: ECO on Mixtral-8x22B (141B) and DeepSeek-V2-Chat (236B), weights unchanged (studies_by_size['>100B'] = 1; 2406.07933). Robustness is untested: coverage_by_operation.attack.by_size has no '>100B' key.
suggested_status.reason:
Version A is a conjunction, and its parts get different levels. C rests on the robustness clause, and it holds only if few-example fine-tuning or white-box edits count as simple attacks. Per the rules, the original sources (2403.03218 RMU/WMDP; 2310.02238 WHP) get no verdicts.

Author overlap:
- Headers flag shared authors for 2408.15221 (4 with 2403.03218, including its first author), 2410.02760 (one with 2403.03218) and 2502.05209 (3 with 2402.16835, none with 2403.03218 or 2310.02238).
- The TAR study 2408.00761 shares 7 authors with 2403.03218.
- 2408.15221, 2410.02760 and 2408.00761 therefore count as R1 for A. 2502.05209 is independent of A's originals but not of 2402.16835.
- The other three behind counts versions.A.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 7 share authors with 2402.16835, per the checks: 2407.15549 (five authors), 2410.12949 (the FLU authors) and 2505.09500 (Hadfield-Menell). The status cites none of them.
- The studies index flags these seven SAME GROUP and no other study cited here. Neither 2408.06223 nor 2611.03955 is flagged, so the re-implementation side of R2 for forgetting at 1-10B and the R2 at 10-100B keep their other-group basis.

Forgetting with general ability kept (R2 at 1-10B and 10-100B):
- Other groups re-evaluate the original's released cais/Zephyr_RMU checkpoint, so this is one checkpoint, not separate RMU runs. Łucki et al.: WMDP-Bio 64.4→29.9, MMLU 58.1→57.1 (2409.18025#R1, #R7). 2608.22527: Bio 0.6591→0.3166 (#r06), MMLU 0.5869→0.5761 (#r26) (fractions).
- 2408.06223 re-implements RMU. On Zephyr-7B at layer 7: Bio 63.7→28.8, Cyber 43.5→28.8, MMLU 58.1→56.8.
- 2408.06223's other families use Adaptive RMU only, at selected early layers (Bio/Cyber, then MMLU against base): Yi-6B l=7 26.1/25.5, MMLU 56.5 (base 60.0); Llama-3-8B l=5 28.2/24.5, MMLU 59.7 (base 62.0); Mistral-7B l=5 27.6/24.8, MMLU 54.9 (base 58.7).
- In 2408.06223, other early layers fail (Yi l=8 Bio 63.3; Llama l=10 Bio 65.1) or cost MMLU (Mistral l=10 47.4). It runs no recovery attack.
- 10-100B: PINT on Llama-3-70B (2611.03955).
- R1 only: ELM reaches Bio 28.7–33.7 on models up to Llama3-70B (2410.02760). RMU on Llama-3-8B-Instruct gives Bio 70.7→28.0 and MMLU 63.8→61.3 (figure-only; 2408.15221).

Robustness clause (C, if few-example fine-tuning or white-box edits count as simple attacks):
- The original ran GCG on Yi-34B RMU only (one reworded prompt per domain, qualitative) and tested Zephyr RMU only with QA and linear probes. Its Appendix B.6 reports that fine-tuning on the cyber forget corpus recovers WMDP-Cyber on Mistral-7B RMU (figure-only).
- So C here is not a failed replication of the original's GCG test. No other group in these records attacks the Yi-34B checkpoint.
- On the released Zephyr RMU checkpoint, an independent group restores Bio to 62.4 with 5 forget-set examples (2409.18025#R14), to 61.6 with 10 retain-set examples (#R10) and to 64.7 by direction ablation (its verdict), against 64.4 unprotected.
- Its enhanced GCG prefix gives 53.9 (#R41). But 2608.22527 runs Łucki et al.'s code on the same checkpoint and gets only 0.3166→0.3637 (#r46).
- Other groups recover other near-chance WMDP checkpoints by fine-tuning: 0.24–0.32→0.57–0.71 for every method except TAR (2502.05209); Openwebtext in all 12 Zephyr/Llama LLMU/RMU pairs (2411.12103); GSM8K SFT (lw:LLebzjrxuRzji6zhk). lw:LLebzjrxuRzji6zhk also recovers checkpoints by forget-representation ablation.
- Quantization on MUSE-News: 4-bit RTN raises KnowMem for GA_GDR 28.9→50.1 and GA_KLR 27.1→50.9 (retrain 33.1, target 63.9). 8-bit leaves them near full precision, at 26.9 and 29.0 (2410.16454). KnowMem has no chance level, and these checkpoints sat at about retrain level, not near chance.
- Partial or no recovery: rephrasing, translation and 5-shot prompts lift 0.030–0.146 to 0.293–0.396, against originals of 0.646–0.710 (2411.12103; the checker reads this verdict as limits_scope). DIA, Crescendo and few-shot QA do not recover the released checkpoint (2608.22527). RepNoise, RR and K-FADE gain 1–2 points under input-space attacks (2502.05209).
- Same group as the original (R1): human multi-turn red teaming recovers 51.2% of 43 free-response questions on RMU Llama-3-8B-Instruct. Six automated attacks recover 2.3–11.6% each, and 25.6% as an ensemble (2408.15221).

Artifact arguments against the 'near chance' part:
- LLMU's answered-only accuracy is 0.689, against the original's 0.665 (2411.12103#r14).
- WHP scores 58.6 on HP-MCQ, against 66.4 for the original model and 25 for chance (2410.02760#r26).
- 2402.16835, which challenges WHP, is itself tagged as an original source in these records.

Counts:

suggested_status.open_questions:
- Never-trained reference under the same attack: give a never-trained, data-filtered or retrained model above 6.9B the same fine-tuning or GCG attack as the unlearned models on WMDP-type knowledge (listed as untested). At 6.9B on WMDP-Bio, data-filtered Deep Ignorance base models are over an order of magnitude more resistant to adversarial fine-tuning than post-training CB and CB+LAT (2508.06601; stated in text, values figure only). Part of filtering's fine-tuning resistance depends on weight scale: under one 293-update plain-SGD epoch, Q/K rescaling closes the strong-filter model's training-accuracy lag behind the unfiltered model, and its held-out gap to the unfiltered model narrows from 14.7 to 6.0 points (2610.09004). If the reference gains as much as the unlearned models, much of the 'recovery' is ordinary learning, which weakens the C reading. If it gains far less, C stands.
- Enhanced GCG on the released Zephyr RMU checkpoint gives 29.9→53.9 in 2409.18025 against 0.3166→0.3637 in 2608.22527, with the same attack code. A matched rerun (template, prefix, steps) would settle whether optimised prompts recover it.
- Untested large models: attack the original's own Yi-34B and Mixtral-8x7B RMU checkpoints, and any model above 100B. The original's GCG test on Yi-34B was qualitative, with one reworded prompt per domain. Such attacks would set the robustness level above 10B, which now rests on few attack studies (counts: coverage_by_operation.attack.by_size['10-100B'] = 4).
- Defining 'simple attacks': fix an attacker budget and access level. If 'simple' means black-box, input-space and no optimisation, RMU's robustness on the released checkpoint reads closer to R2 at 1-10B (2608.22527; Łucki's simple jailbreaks; 2506.10236 Hindi filler on RMU). The same-group human red-teaming result (2408.15221) counts against that reading. If 'simple' includes few-example fine-tuning or white-box edits, it reads C. The original itself reports fine-tuning recovery on Mistral-7B RMU.
- RMU on Llama-3-8B gives near chance with MMLU kept, incomplete forgetting, or near chance with MMLU collapse, depending on the study (2408.15221, 2603.01792, 2608.22527). Matched-hyperparameter reruns would show whether forgetting with ability kept transfers beyond Zephyr.
- Newer methods that report near chance with MMLU kept but run no attack (ALTER, PINT, TRACE and others): if they resist fine-tuning, ablation and quantization at matched utility in independent hands, a method-specific R2 'unlearning works' becomes possible.

original_result.setup: The study applied RMU, an unlearning method designed to suppress targeted knowledge, to biology and cybersecurity knowledge, then measured accuracy on those subjects and general ability.
original_result.result: On Zephyr-7B, RMU lowered accuracy on WMDP-Bio (biology knowledge) from 63.7% to 31.2% and on WMDP-Cyber (cybersecurity knowledge) from 44.0% to 28.2%. Accuracy on MMLU, a general knowledge benchmark, changed from 58.1% to 57.1%.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

These are ALTER, ASU, PINT (TOFU linear probe only), TRACE, SRMU, MPSelectTune, OFMU, LIRA, GUARD-IT, ADU, Cascade and R2MU. 2606.10338 runs no attack of any kind, and in it only TRACE keeps MMLU: 0.5819/0.5541 against Origin 0.5954/0.5672 (Qwen1.5-MoE/DeepSeek-V2-Lite). ESFT (0.5319/0.5099) and SEUF (0.4915/0.4553) also reach near-chance WMDP without being attacked but lose more MMLU. The authors say SEUF's setting can degrade utility. FALCON, NSRU and SSPU face only prompt-level attacks that leave the weights unchanged; FALCON's enhanced GCG uses white-box gradients.

wording_issues.issue: Many forget measures have no chance level, so studies compare against other references. The original WHP reports completion familiarity 0.290→0.007 at 80 steps, and its untested line says familiarity has no chance level. GA forget ROUGE-L starts at only 0.062–0.152 before unlearning (2611.05272). Forget exact match is judged against a Retrain floor of 0.0735, with GA reaching 0.0070 from 0.6996 (2609.05976). MUSE KnowMem is ROUGE on QA, not accuracy (2410.16454's untested line). Other references in use are TOFU KS-test forget quality, Gold or retrained models, and judge scores.

A near-chance MCQ score can come from collapse, refusal or an inference filter rather than from removal, or the model can start near chance. NPO on Zephyr-7B stays at 26% on WMDP-bio, with 94.2% refusals and gibberish (2511.04934). The authors' own RMU run on Llama-3-8B (stage not stated) reaches Bio target accuracy 0.2498 while MMLU falls 0.6008→0.4022, and is at 0.2812 under GCG (fractions; 2608.22527). ALU brings Llama-3 8B to WMDP Bio/Chem/Cyber 26.31/25.12/24.76 because a random-option agent answers flagged questions (2502.00406). On SciQ-WMDP-Bio, Llama-2 starts at 19.7% and Mistral-7B at 35.3% before unlearning (2607.03932).

Low accuracy can come from non-answering or degenerate output rather than lost knowledge. Zephyr LLMU answered accuracy on WMDP-Bio is 0.689 against 0.665 before unlearning, while zero-shot accuracy sits at or below chance (fractions; 2411.12103). RMU on gemma-2-2b keeps outputting gibberish under a suffix attack, on one sampled question (2503.11127). For RT Full on LLaMA3, QA recall falls 76.4→13.4 while fill-in-the-blank falls only 85.9→72.7; the authors say memorization probes still detect the knowledge and RT usually refuses to answer (2406.10890). NPO-family near-chance MCQ hides over-forgetting (ES 0.02), and GSM8K falls 0.76→0.03 (text; 2510.07626).

Many tested targets are behaviours, tasks, strings or non-text concepts, not knowledge scored by accuracy. Examples: harmful-response rate (Llama 2 GA 54%→2%; 2310.10683), a whole benchmark task (GSM8K to 0.017 on Llama 2 70b; 2408.04140), judge-audited deception on sycophancy items (2609.38909), and image-concept attack success in diffusion models (2405.19237). Other examples: PII extraction, verbatim memorization, deprecated-API use, protein fitness, speaker identity, robot skills, and image classes.

The result depends on question format and template. On sports facts (Table 1, model not named), Attribution Patching localization brings standard forget accuracy to 0.000, but MCQ original-answer accuracy stays at 0.767; FLU, Nonlocalized and All-MLPs also reach about 0 standard forget, with MCQ at 0.110–0.279 (2410.12949). TAR-Bio-v1 scores 24.0 on official WMDP-Bio but 39.8 with no chat template plus BOS (2412.07097). For WHP+, open-ended forget ROUGE-L falls 53.04→21.01, but MCQ accuracy is 36.73 against chance 20 and original 74.26 (2505.02884). On OFFSIDE, Qwen2.5-VL-7B GA MCQ stays at 62.7% against 64.4% while generation is suppressed (2510.22535). Multi-hop, inverse and image-conditioned probes give similar gaps.

Clean MMLU can hide losses elsewhere. NPO keeps MMLU at 0.51 against 0.64, but GSM8K falls 0.76→0.03 (text; 2510.07626). On gemma-2-2b-it, GA moves MMLU 56.83→50.94 while GSM8K falls 43.75→0.76 (2505.24428). RMU keeps MMLU at 55.22 on Llama, but it falls to 22.95 when WMDP content is in context (text; 2603.00823, unchecked: its source check was not returned). Swapping one wrong MMLU choice for 'SARS-CoV-2' cuts RMU retain accuracy about 28% while the base model improves (2410.02879).

Knowledge next to the target is often lost even when broad MMLU holds. The original's own Zephyr RMU rows show MMLU Virology 52.4→25.9 and Computer Security 65.0→45.0 (2403.03218). Adaptive RMU on Zephyr-7B with in-domain retain sets collapses MMLU to about 30 where forgetting reaches chance, and leaves Bio at 62.6 where MMLU is kept; in its subset-unlearning setting at layer 7, MMLU-Retain falls 58.9→39.4 (2408.06223). At the ATU 20% checkpoint, Align-then-Unlearn lowers neighbour knowledge 61.4→52.3 while MMLU stays 64.4→64.5 (2506.13181). NPO and GA degrade facts from semantically similar articles at a rate similar to the targets (figure only; 2606.13873).

The attacks reported as recovering knowledge vary widely in budget and access, and the statement sets no limit on either. They run from fine-tuning on one 2-example batch (2407.15549) to 250M tokens of SFT on an instruction mixture with life-science subsets removed, which lifts Gemma 4 (26B-A4B) RMU WMDP-Bio 29.2→60.8, against 78.8 for the original after the same SFT (2610.25791). They also run from black-box rephrasing to human multi-turn red teaming with unlimited time and 240 total hours, which recovers 51.2% of 43 questions (2408.15221), and to white-box GCG or embedding optimisation. Some operations that partly recover fit none of versions B–E: 50% magnitude pruning raises Zephyr-7B-beta GradDiff WMDP-Bio 0.25→0.35, against 0.64 for the dense original, while MMLU falls 0.43→0.35 (fractions; no pruned-original control; 2602.00577). Repeated sampling also recovers knowledge.

Recovery is graded, the reference point varies across studies, and the statement sets no threshold. Some recovery is partial. Relearning without direct answers lifts RMU MCQ 0.3086→0.4812 against a pre-unlearning 0.5177 (2406.13356), and the best input-space attack lifts RMU 0.26→0.34 against 0.70 (2502.05209), all fractions. Reference models also rise under attack: on TOFU, Retrain reaches leak@128 0.622, against NPO 0.745 and Original 0.886 (2511.04934). Some attacks overshoot the original: after 75 relearning steps, MUSE-News VerbMem reaches 73.2 (GradDiff) and 78.9 (SimNPO) against Original 56.3 (2609.36612).

The same named method gives different results depending on implementation, model and settings. RMU on Llama-3-8B reaches 28.0% WMDP-Bio on the Instruct model (2408.15221) but 49.4 on Llama3-8B in ALTER's comparator run at benchmark defaults (2603.01792). The unlearn layer decides the outcome. On Llama-3-8B, where only Adaptive RMU is run (base Bio 71.2), Bio is near chance only at layers 5–7 (28.2, 27.8, 29.3); it is 46.4/45.3 at layers 3–4, 65.1 at layer 10 and 70.4 at layer 31. Plain RMU's layer sweep is reported only for Zephyr: effective at layers 3–10, not at 11–31 (2408.06223). Under one attack in one study, methods split: Hindi filler raises ELM logit accuracy from about 0.29–0.34 to 0.47–0.59, while Zephyr_RMU goes 0.3071→0.3009 (2506.10236).

method_sensitivity.factor: Unlearning configuration: layer, depth, retain set, which parameters are updated, stopping and selection rule
method_sensitivity.what: Layer: plain RMU on Zephyr-7B works at unlearn layers 3–10 but not at 11–31 (2408.06223). The same study's Adaptive RMU behaves differently by model. On Llama-3-8B, WMDP-Bio stays at 65.1 at layer 10 and 70.4 at layer 31 (base 71.2). On Yi-6B (layers 11–15, 19) and Mistral-7B (layers 11, 15, 17) it reaches Bio 25.4–27.6, with MMLU 57.0 at Yi layer 13 (base 60.0) and 56.7 at Mistral layer 17 (base 58.7). Depth: under the same relearning attack, deep vs shallow configurations give revival of 0.025 vs 0.800 (GradDiff) and 0.000 vs 0.695 (RMU). Retain set, Zephyr-7B: with a WikiText retain set, RMU, Adaptive RMU and SRMU reach a WMDP average of 26.0–28.4. A same-domain retain set leaves RMU at 44.8 and Adaptive RMU at 43.54, with MMLU 58.5→51.9/51.15 (2512.16297). With in-domain WMDP retain sets, Adaptive RMU reaches Bio 28.1 (layer 6) and 29.6 (layer 10), but MMLU is 30.1 and 29.3 (2408.06223). Stopping: DUSK stops at the first epoch where URK falls below 70, which leaves UFK at 24.3–55.1 against Retrain 5.2.

method_sensitivity.factor: Forget-set construction and target properties (curation, size, popularity, inter-connectivity, how the knowledge was acquired)
method_sensitivity.what: Curation: SimNPO is held fixed and run separately on each curator's forget set. Evaluation-aware curation lets it suppress 96.2–100% of forget extraction. BM25 or Infini-gram retrieval curation gives 12.7–47.8% on four models and 1.0–2.8% on Qwen3-8B and Olmo-3-7B. Popularity and acquisition, LLaMA-3.1-8B with GA: forget ROUGE-L rises 0.766→0.918 for popular facts on the pretrained model. It falls 0.935→0.206 for popular facts after SFT and 0.691→0.476 for rare facts on the pretrained model. Retraining on one split restores held-out accuracy for facts learned in pretraining (Years, MMLU, WMDP-deduped), but not for synthetic random-birthday facts fine-tuned in (one dataset). Size, TOFU, four baseline methods (GA, GD, KL, PO): with a 1% forget set, utility stays stable but forgetting is partial. Forget quality is <0.001 on Phi-1.5 and at most 0.01 on Llama-2-7B, below the 0.05 threshold. With 5% and 10% sets, utility drops severely and models with high forget quality are unusable.

method_sensitivity.factor: Attack type (including attack-side reparameterization), attacker access and attack strength
method_sensitivity.what: RMU on Llama-3-8B-Instruct (WMDP-Bio): the best input-space attack gives 0.26→0.34 and the best tampering attack 0.26→0.57. A separately trained RMU checkpoint of the same base model (WMDP-Bio MCQ 70.7→28.0%) was tested on 43 WMDP-Bio free-response questions. Human multi-turn red teaming recovers 51.2%, against 2.3–11.6% for each of six automated attacks and 25.6% for their ensemble. Steering Zephyr-RMU along weight-difference directions lifts WMDP-Bio 31.2→56.2 at an 8.54% false-positive rate, but only to 39.7 at 0.94%. LUNAR on Llama-2-7B (PISTOL, pass@1 about 0.05): oracle SVD ablation, which needs the original weights, gives 1.00. Blind difference-in-means ablation at layer 22, alpha 0.5, gives 0.45.

method_sensitivity.factor: Relearning data (relevance, source, fraction) and attack budget
method_sensitivity.what: The choice of relearning data, and how much of it, changes recovery. Related vs general text (ROUGE-L recall): Llama-2-7b WHP SCRUB .1833→.4224 with related text vs .3701 with general text; Zephyr WMDP GA .1217→.3096 vs .1666. Steps: MUSE-Books NPO KnowMem is 0.333 after 50 relearning steps and 34.126 after 100 (original 45.879). Harmful vs benign data: FaithUn GD on Llama-3.2 3B (chance 33.3) reaches 48.13 after harmful forget-subset fine-tuning at p=0.1 and 54.76 at p=0.3, but 33.33 after benign Alpaca. VoiceBox TGU, attacked with the forgotten speakers' own audio (audio amount and steps change together): 1 min per speaker over 14.5K steps leaves SIM-F at 0.162 (0.169 before attack). 15 min over 36.25K steps gives 0.735 (original 0.708). Both attacks degrade the retained speakers (SIM-R 0.226 and 0.303; WER-R 4.61 and 4.23). The authors call the 15-min result speaker-specific transfer learning, not restoration of the original model. There is no never-exposed control.

method_sensitivity.factor: Quantization bit width, scheme, and the unlearning method or optimizer
method_sensitivity.what: MUSE-News (LLaMA-2 7B): GA_KLR KnowMem goes 27.1→50.9/49.8/49.3 under 4-bit RTN/AWQ/GPTQ, but 27.1→29.0 under 8-bit RTN. NPO_KLR goes 36.6→37.2 at 8-bit. LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct on TOFU: adapter-space INT4 raises forget accuracy (GA 0.028→0.262), INT8 gives 0.000, and merged-model NF4 lowers it (GA 0.070→0.014). INT4 recovery also depends on the unlearning method: recovery rate is 86.9 for NPO on Qwen3-32B and 0.0 for PALU and AS. MUSE-Books NPO under 4-bit: VerbMem goes 0→48.5 when trained with Adam and stays at 0→0 with the Hybrid optimizer. Under 100-step relearning, though, the Hybrid model recovers KnowMem 0→31.3 and VerbMem 0→32.3 (figure values).

method_sensitivity.factor: Decoding: greedy vs sampling, sampling budget and temperature
method_sensitivity.what: WHP model on Harry Potter Q&A: greedy decoding shows no leakage, but under top-p sampling (1024 samples) 38% of questions have a leak-probability upper bound above 10%. On the same model, top-k sampling (100 samples per question, temperature 2) recovers 27.8% against 3.6% one-shot. TOFU NPO on LLaMA-3.2-1B-Instruct at T=p=1.0: leak@k–ES is 0.206 at k=1 and 0.745 at k=128, against Retrain 0.169 and 0.622. RMU WMDP-bio judge leakage is near zero at T=p=0.2 and rises at T=p=1.0 (figure). leak@1000 raises IDKDPO from 28 to 58 (WMDP-Bio, Llama-3-8B-Instruct) and SimNPO from 2.00 to 45.25 (TOFU-10%).

method_sensitivity.factor: Knowledge measure, answer extraction, chat template and scorer
method_sensitivity.what: LLMU on Zephyr WMDP-Bio: zero-shot accuracy is at or below chance, but accuracy on answered items is 0.689, against the original's 0.665. TAR-Bio-v1 scores 24.0 on WMDP-Bio in the official format, 39.8 with no chat template plus BOS, and 35.4 with chat template plus BOS. TAR-Bio-v2 scores 28.1 in the official format and 24.3–25.1 in the other three formats (Table 7). OFFSIDE (Qwen2.5-VL-7B): after GA, forget-set 4-choice accuracy stays near vanilla (62.7% vs 64.4%) while generation is suppressed. Qwen3-VL-8B: exact-match scoring gives GA/NPO disclosure drops of 0.192/0.210, and a semantic scorer gives a lower bound of 0.040.

method_sensitivity.factor: Query form, language and input modality
method_sensitivity.what: On GONE, Mistral GA reaches direct UE 0.985 but inverse UE 0.322, below the pre-unlearning 0.364. InternVL3-8B on Hateful Memes: forget accuracy after NPO/RMU is 39.41/59.99 with text queries but 73.30/77.06 with image-conditioned queries. LLaMa3-8B fake news: when English-source data is unlearned in English, 94% of fake responses are removed in every query language. For non-English-source data, same-language unlearning removes 97% in that language, but English queries give 11% more fake responses. After matched source-language forgetting, native routes in other languages keep about 18% (SimNPO) and 36% (RMU) of the target.

method_sensitivity.factor: Unlearning method under the same attack
method_sensitivity.what: Hindi filler text raises ELM's WMDP-bio logit accuracy from about 0.29–0.34 to 0.47–0.59, but leaves Zephyr_RMU at 0.3071→0.3009. leak@1000 on WMDP-Bio: GradDiff 21→24, IDKNLL 32→66. TOFU relearning with 40 examples raises Forget KnowMem by +0.15 for SHRED, +0.47 for NPO and +0.67 for RMU, against +0.05 for the retrained Target. Enhanced GCG on Llama-3-8B (stage not stated), WMDP-Bio: the authors' own RMU run goes 0.2498→0.2812 and their own simNPO run 0.2608→0.6009. The ELM authors' released checkpoint goes 0.3323→0.4910.

RMU, run as a comparator at benchmark defaults, reaches WMDP-Bio 30.2 on Zephyr-7B (from 64.4) but leaves Llama3-8B at 49.4 (from 71.2), with Llama MMLU 62.1→40.1. In another study, RMU keeps Zephyr-7B MMLU (0.5869→0.5761) but drops Llama-3-8B (stage not stated) MMLU from 0.6008 to 0.4022 (Bio run) and 0.2302 (Cyber run). There the Zephyr model is the released cais checkpoint and the Llama models are the authors' own runs with separate Bio/Cyber hyperparameters, so family is confounded with checkpoint source. After GA, benign Alpaca fine-tuning gives FaithUn forget accuracy 16.71 on Llama-3.2 3B but 63.64 on Qwen-2.5 3B (chance 33.3). Relearning on concept-related text restores 93–103% of baseline accuracy on Llama-3.1-8b-it, against 79–85% on Gemma-2-2b-it, for ELM, RMU and AlphaEdit. The 95% CIs overlap across the two models for ELM and RMU.
